newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh Balkhashmys copper plant sees '97 output up.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh Balkhashmys copper plant sees '97 output up.

text.p: Kazakhstan's Balkhash Mining and Metallurgical Combine plans to boost production of copper cathodes to 103,000 tonnes in 1997 against 78,700 tonnes in 1996, the plant's technical director said on Monday.

"We think we will be able to stabilise production in May so that by the end of the year we can get to the necessary level of production," Nikolai Levchenko, the plant's technical director, told Reuters by telephone. He said blister copper output would increase to 110,000 tonnes in 1997 over 67,050 tonnes last year.

The troubled plant was sold to Korea's Samsung Corp in February. The Korean group has promised to invest $700 million by 2000 to improve plant, develop new ore basins and boost output to 200,000 tonnes of copper per year.
Samsung is the third company to have taken on the ailing plant, where reserves are nearly exhausted and which owes $200 million in debts.
Output at Balkhashmys, which produces about 40 percent of the former Soviet republic's copper, slumped from 135,000 tonnes in 1995 to 78,700 tonnes last year.

Levchenko said production of cathodes in March over February had more than tripled since Samsung took over management, while production of blister copper had increased four-fold in the same period. He declined to give further figures.
